priv.body:
This website is run by BOBBY AC REPAIR & HOME APPLIANCE SERVICES, Narasaraopet, Andhra Pradesh. We respect your privacy and collect as little information as possible.

What we collect

The website does not have user accounts and does not store your booking details on a server. When you use the booking form, your details are placed into a WhatsApp message on your own device. Nothing is sent until you choose to send it.

How we use your details

Information you send by phone or WhatsApp (such as your name, number, area and appliance problem) is used only to arrange and carry out your service. We do not sell or share it for marketing.

Third-party services

The site loads fonts from Google Fonts, and a map from Google Maps. These services may receive basic technical information such as your IP address. WhatsApp is governed by its own privacy policy.

Your language choice

We save your chosen language in your browser so the site remembers it. You can clear it at any time from your browser settings.

Location

If you tap “Use my current location” or pick a point on the map, the location stays in the booking form on your device. It is added to your WhatsApp message as a map link and reaches us only if you send that message. The map is provided by OpenStreetMap.

Contact

For any privacy question, call or WhatsApp +91 83748 89163.

sp.id.h: How to Identify the Correct AC Spare Part
sp.id.sub: Most wrong-part problems come from guessing. These steps help us match the exact part the first time.
sp.id.1.d: The sticker on the side of the indoor unit and on the outdoor unit shows the brand, model number, capacity, refrigerant (R32, R410A or R22) and voltage.
sp.id.2.d: Inverter ACs use different PCBs, compressors and fan motors. A non-inverter part will not work in an inverter unit, and the reverse.
sp.id.3.d: Capacitors show MFD and voltage, motors show wattage and rotation, PCBs carry a part code. Matching these values matters more than the brand name.
sp.id.4.d: Take photos of the part, its label and its wiring from two angles. This avoids wiring mistakes when the new part is fitted.
sp.id.5.d: Symptoms often overlap — a dead outdoor unit can be a capacitor, contactor, PCB or wiring fault. Replacing a part without testing wastes money.
sp.safe: AC units carry mains voltage, and capacitors can hold a charge even after the power is switched off. Compressor, coil, valve and gas work involves pressurised refrigerant and brazing. Please do not open the AC or attempt these replacements yourself — have a trained technician do it.

post.why-is-my-ac-not-cooling.title: Why Is My AC Not Cooling Properly?
post.why-is-my-ac-not-cooling.excerpt: The most common reasons an AC runs but does not cool, and what you can safely check yourself.
post.why-is-my-ac-not-cooling.body:
An AC that runs but does not cool is the most common complaint we hear in Narasaraopet summers. The good news: the cause is often simple. Here are the usual reasons, from easiest to most serious.

1. Dirty air filters

Dust-clogged filters block airflow, so the room never gets cold. Filters in a split AC can be slid out and rinsed with plain water every two to three weeks in heavy use. Let them dry fully before refitting.

2. Wrong settings

Check the remote is on Cool mode (not Fan or Dry) and the temperature is set around 24°C. A very low setting does not cool faster; it only makes the compressor work longer.

3. Dirty or blocked outdoor unit

The outdoor unit releases heat. If it sits in direct afternoon sun, is covered with dust, or is boxed in by walls, cooling drops sharply. Keep the area around it clear.

4. Low refrigerant (gas)

If the gas has leaked, cooling becomes weak and you may see ice on the copper pipes. Gas does not get "used up", so low gas always means a leak that must be found and repaired before refilling.

5. Electrical or component faults

A weak capacitor, a faulty sensor or a PCB problem can stop the compressor from running properly. These need a technician with the right tools.

When to call a technician

If cleaning the filters and checking the settings does not help, book an inspection. Please do not open the electrical panel yourself.
post.when-should-you-service-your-ac.tit: When Should You Service Your Air Conditioner?
post.when-should-you-service-your-ac.exc: A simple servicing schedule for hot, dusty Andhra summers, and the signs your AC is overdue.
post.when-should-you-service-your-ac.bod:
Regular servicing keeps an AC cooling well, reduces power use and catches small faults before they become expensive. In a hot, dusty town like Narasaraopet, ACs work harder than the manufacturer's average, so timing matters.

A practical schedule

  • Before summer (February–March): a full service so the AC is ready for peak heat.
  • After heavy summer use (around July–August): a second service if the AC runs most of the day.
  • Filters: rinse every two to three weeks during heavy use.

Signs your AC needs servicing now

  • It takes much longer to cool the room
  • A musty or bad smell when it starts
  • Water dripping from the indoor unit
  • Unusual rattling or humming sounds
  • Your electricity bill has gone up without a reason

What a proper service includes

Cleaning the filters and indoor unit, clearing the drain line, checking the outdoor unit and fan, and checking that the AC is cooling as it should. If the technician finds a deeper problem, they should explain it and give you an estimate before doing any extra work.
AC Gas Filling: When Is It Actually Required?
Gas is not a routine top-up. Learn the real signs of low gas and why a leak check must come first.

"Your AC needs gas" is one of the most common things people hear when their AC is not cooling. Sometimes it is true. Often, it is not. Here is how to tell the difference.

AC gas does not run out on its own

The refrigerant in your AC moves in a sealed loop. It is not burned or used up like petrol. If the gas level is low, there is a leak somewhere: at a joint, a valve or a damaged pipe.

Signs that may point to low gas

  • Cooling has slowly become weaker over weeks
  • Ice or frost on the copper pipes or indoor coil
  • A hissing or bubbling sound near the pipes
  • The outdoor unit runs but the air inside is only slightly cool

Problems that look the same but are not gas

Dirty filters, a clogged indoor coil, a dusty outdoor unit, a weak capacitor or a faulty fan motor can all cause poor cooling. Filling gas will not fix any of these.

The right order of work

  1. Inspect the AC and measure the pressure
  2. Find and repair the leak if there is one
  3. Fill gas to the correct level for your model
  4. Test the cooling performance

Ask your technician to explain which of these steps your AC needs before you agree to gas filling.
post.why-is-your-ac-leaking-water.title: Why Is Your AC Leaking Water?
post.why-is-your-ac-leaking-water.excerp: Water dripping from the indoor unit is common and usually fixable. Here are the causes.
post.why-is-your-ac-leaking-water.body:
An AC removes moisture from the room air. That water is meant to flow out through a drain pipe, usually outside the wall. When it drips from the indoor unit instead, one of these is usually the reason.

Blocked drain pipe

Dust and algae can block the drain line, especially if the AC has not been serviced for a while. The water backs up and overflows from the indoor unit. This is the most common cause and is cleared during servicing.

Dirty filters causing ice

Clogged filters reduce airflow, the coil gets too cold and forms ice. When the ice melts, more water than the tray can handle drips into the room.

Incorrect installation slope

The indoor unit must tilt slightly towards the drain side. If it was mounted perfectly level or tilted the wrong way, water collects and leaks.

Damaged drain tray or pipe

A cracked tray or a disconnected or kinked pipe will leak even when everything else is fine.

What to do

Switch the AC off if water is reaching electrical points or furniture, wipe the area dry, and book a service. Most leaks are fixed by cleaning the drain line and filters or correcting the unit's slope.
post.split-ac-vs-window-ac.title: Split AC vs Window AC: Which Suits Your Home?
post.split-ac-vs-window-ac.excerpt: A plain comparison of installation, noise, cooling and upkeep to help you choose.
post.split-ac-vs-window-ac.body:
Both split and window ACs cool a room well when they are the right size and properly installed. The best choice depends on your room, your walls and your budget.

Window AC

  • One single unit fitted in a window or a wall opening
  • Usually lower purchase and installation cost
  • Simpler to remove and shift
  • Louder, because the compressor sits in the same unit
  • Needs a suitable window or opening

Split AC

  • Indoor unit on the wall, outdoor unit outside, joined by copper pipes
  • Much quieter inside the room
  • More placement options and a cleaner look
  • Installation needs piping, drilling and correct gas handling
  • Generally better suited to larger rooms

Quick guide

Choose a window AC for a small room with a suitable window, rented homes, or a tight budget. Choose a split AC when you want quiet cooling, a larger room, or the room has no suitable window.

Installation matters for both

Correct mounting, sealing, drain slope and electrical connection decide how well and how long your AC works. Whichever type you choose, get it installed and tested properly.
post.how-to-maintain-your-refrigerator.e: Easy habits that keep your fridge cooling well, plus the warning signs that need a technician.
post.how-to-maintain-your-refrigerator.b:
A refrigerator runs 24 hours a day, every day. A few simple habits keep it cooling well, save electricity and help it last longer.

Give it space to breathe

Leave a gap of a few inches between the back of the fridge and the wall so heat can escape. Keep it away from the stove and direct sunlight.

Keep the door seal clean

Wipe the rubber gasket with a damp cloth. If the door does not close firmly or the seal is torn, cold air leaks out and the compressor works harder.

Do not overload it

Cold air needs to circulate. Packing shelves tightly or blocking the vents inside causes uneven cooling. Let hot food cool down before putting it in.

Clean the back and the drain

Dust on the condenser at the back reduces cooling. Unplug the fridge before gently cleaning it. In frost-free models, a blocked drain hole causes water to collect at the bottom.

Signs you need a technician

  • The fridge runs but does not cool, or the freezer cools but the fridge does not
  • Water collecting inside or under the fridge
  • Loud clicking, buzzing or the compressor running non-stop
  • Heavy ice build-up in a frost-free model
